proof:
Source: the finiteness part of step 5 of the parent proof (K is compact, so only finitely many faces meet it). The statement allows any ι, not necessarily injective, and the closed cube. So the bound on b below is ⌈ρ⌉ + k rather than the parent's ρ + 1, which relies on ι being injective. Only finiteness is used.

Notation: e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ). For p = (ι, b), Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) + Σ_j y_j • e_{ι(j)}, so Φ_p(y)_i = b_i + S_i with S_i := Σ_j (if i = ι(j) then y_j else 0). Coordinate formula, used throughout: Φ_p(y)_i = b_i + Σ_j (if i = ι(j) then y_j else 0). In Lean, state it as a local `have` inside the theorem (a leaf may add no separate lemma) and prove it by `simp only [PiLp.add_apply, WithLp.ofLp_sum, Finset.sum_apply, PiLp.smul_apply, PiLp.single_apply, smul_eq_mul, mul_ite, mul_one, mul_zero]`. Plain `simp` gets stuck on `Pi.single`, and EuclideanSpace.single_apply is deprecated in favour of PiLp.single_apply.

1. (K is bounded.) K is compact, hence bounded. So there is ρ ∈ ℝ with ‖x‖ ≤ ρ for every x ∈ K (IsCompact.isBounded, Bornology.IsBounded.exists_norm_le). For every x ∈ ℝ^P and every i, |x_i| ≤ ‖x‖ (PiLp.norm_apply_le).
2. (Coordinate shifts.) If y ∈ [0,1]^k, then 0 ≤ S_i ≤ k for every i. Each summand is y_j ∈ [0, 1] or 0, so it lies in [0, 1], and there are k summands (Finset.sum_nonneg, Finset.sum_le_sum, Σ_{j : Fin k} 1 = k).
3. (Bounds on b.) Let p = (ι, b) be in the set, witnessed by y ∈ [0,1]^k with x := Φ_p(y) ∈ K. For each i, |b_i + S_i| = |x_i| ≤ ρ by step 1, so −ρ ≤ b_i + S_i ≤ ρ (abs_le). Put N := ⌈ρ⌉ + k ∈ ℤ. Using ρ ≤ ⌈ρ⌉ (Int.le_ceil), 0 ≤ k and step 2:
   - b_i ≤ ρ − S_i ≤ ρ ≤ ⌈ρ⌉ ≤ N;
   - b_i ≥ −ρ − S_i ≥ −ρ − k ≥ −(⌈ρ⌉ + k) = −N.
   So b_i ∈ [−N, N] for every i; cast the real inequalities back to ℤ (exact_mod_cast). This also works when ρ < 0, for example when K = ∅.
4. (Finiteness.) By step 3 the set is contained in Set.univ ×ˢ (Set.univ.pi fun _ => Set.Icc (−N) N) ⊆ (Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ). The first factor is finite (Set.finite_univ; Fin k → Fin P is a Fintype). The second is a finite product of finite integer intervals (Set.Finite.pi, Set.finite_Icc). So the product is finite (Set.Finite.prod), and so is the set (Set.Finite.subset). ∎
key_steps: K compact gives ρ with |x_i| ≤ ‖x‖ ≤ ρ on K.
For y ∈ [0,1]^k, Φ_p(y)_i = b_i + S_i with 0 ≤ S_i ≤ k, so |b_i| ≤ ⌈ρ⌉ + k.
The set lies in (all ι) × [−N, N]^P with N = ⌈ρ⌉ + k, which is finite.
